title: Easy Going Canadian Pork Bake
description: A hearty, comforting Canadian dish featuring pork, rice paper sheets, and a wood-fired bake, perfect for a lazy Sunday, this high-protein-friendly recipe is sure to satisfy your cravings. It is a fatty and pillowy dish that combines the richness of pork with the crunch of rice paper.
instructions: Preheat the wood-fired oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a small bowl, mix together the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the pork shoulder, making sure to coat it evenly.
Wrap the pork shoulder in the rice paper sheets, overlapping the sheets to ensure complete coverage.
Place the wrapped pork shoulder in the wood-fired oven and bake for 6 hours.
After 6 hours, remove the pork from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes.
While the pork is resting, heat the beer in a small saucepan over medium heat until it is warm and syrupy.
Brush the warm beer over the pork shoulder, making sure to coat it evenly.
Return the pork to the oven and bake for an additional 30 minutes.
Remove the pork from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before slicing and serving.
